digest.component_or_area: tickets store compaction, sync, and recovery
propositions: Parallel multi-session writes to the git-backed tickets store cause crashes during operation-linked compaction when the worktree is mutated before git commit, leaving tracked markers and untracked artifacts that prevent future merges and strand commits off origin.

The compaction fold must be crash-atomic via an intent journal sentinel outside the worktree, written before worktree mutation and removed only on completed outcomes or journal-detected recovery, ensuring no dirty tree is produced on worker death.
Sync and push recovery paths must handle both untracked-file collisions and tracked-file deletions/modifications to complete the union merge keeping both parents without orphaning local commits.
Runtime markers (*/.archived, */.write.lock) tracked in HEAD before gitignore patterns existed must be untracked idempotently and removed from the tracked dirt class at source.
Store-wide scans (fsck, compact-all) must default to active-only tickets and accept --include-archived to reach archived ones, scaling scan cost with the active working set.
fsck must detect dirty-tree/stale-lock classes and doctor --repair must heal them under the write lock without modifying .tmp-event-* content.
